summary: @servicetitan/onboarding-ui preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `scripts.preinstall` runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js], {cwd: D})` against a shipped sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle obfuscated with a shuffled string-array decoder (`WV8StW` rotating a large constants array `n7gIxM`) and mangled identifiers, so its behavior is opaque to Node-based inspection. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with hex-mangled identifier names (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and control-flow-flattened proxy objects (`_0x19328d.YCZJE`, `_0x2c3338.NIXVR`), hiding the intent of the install hook. A ServiceTitan React onboarding UI library has no legitimate need for a downloaded alternate runtime to execute a hidden bundle at install time; installing the package on default settings runs attacker-authored obfuscated code on the installer's machine via a runtime specifically dropped to bypass Node-side supply-chain scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
